attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

cases.label: tax and line amounts round half away from zero: 3 x 0.95 x 0.505 % = 0.01438875 -> 0.01
cases.reasoning: TaxAmount = ROUND(PickedQuantity * UnitPrice * TaxRate / 100.0, 2); UnitPrice 0.95 and TaxRate 0.505 both end in 5. Both engines must round half away from zero into decimal(18,2), and ExtendedPrice must be the sum of the two rounded parts.

cases.label: PickingCompletedWhen at the maximum datetime2 (9999-12-31): the order still counts as picked
cases.reasoning: The WHERE requires PickingCompletedWhen IS NOT NULL; a boundary value 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999 must satisfy it on both engines (datetime2 vs timestamp microseconds), so the invoice is generated.

cases.label: empty DeliveryAddressLine1 with NULL DeliveryAddressLine2 makes DeliveryInstructions NULL (+ semantics)
cases.reasoning: DeliveryInstructions = c.DeliveryAddressLine1 + N', ' + c.DeliveryAddressLine2; with line2 NULL the whole concatenation is NULL on SQL Server, and the conversion uses || which also yields NULL (concat() would not). Line1 is '' to keep '' distinct from NULL.

null-vs-empty.detail: empty string: yes; NULL in a text input: yes

cases.label: two invoice lines whose descriptions differ only in case are both written
cases.reasoning: Order lines 'dry' and 'DRY' differ only in case and share PackageTypeID/TaxRate ties; both are inserted into Sales.InvoiceLines verbatim, with no case folding on either engine.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Sales.Orders share PickingCompletedWhen = "2020-01-01T10:00:00.000000"

cases.label: customer purchase order number with a trailing space is carried onto the invoice
cases.reasoning: Invoices copy o.CustomerPurchaseOrderNumber; 'PO-1 ' keeps its trailing space in nvarchar(20) and in the converted varchar(20). A conversion that trimmed it would differ.

cases.label: an order with no lines: its customer-transaction sums are NULL, hitting a NOT NULL violation that rolls everything back
cases.reasoning: SUM over no invoice lines is NULL; Sales.CustomerTransactions.AmountExcludingTax is NOT NULL, so both engines raise and undo every write (the whole batch). The outcome compares the error class, not the message.

cases.label: two orders with non-contiguous ids 1 and 3 are both invoiced; new invoice ids come from the sequence
cases.reasoning: OrderIDs 1 and 3 (a gap) are invoiced together. Each qualifying order consumes one NEXT VALUE FOR Sequences.InvoiceID / nextval; the invoices are matched by OrderID (the assignment of ids to orders is undefined), so both engines must create one invoice per order and leave the same holdings.

objections.text: The supplied arithmetic is 3 * 0.95 * 0.505 / 100 = 0.0143925, not 0.01438875. It rounds and truncates to the same two-decimal value, 0.01, so this input does not test the claimed rounding tie or the planted round-versus-truncation defect.

DeliveryAddressLine2 is NULL, so the entire address expression is NULL whether DeliveryAddressLine1 is '' or NULL. The fixed two-order case already tests NULL line 2. A03 cannot expose a conversion that collapses the supplied empty line 1 to NULL.

The hand-derived 'an order without lines' case has the same requested order, empty Sales.OrderLines table and expected NOT NULL failure with rollback. A06 does not change any input that reaches a different path.
